claim.claim-text: 1. A method of recovering oil from oil-producing microorganisms comprising
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the method does not comprise a pasteurization step.
3. The method of any one of claims 1 to 2, wherein the fermentation medium has a salt concentration from 5 g/L to 20 g/L; and optionally wherein the salt comprises sodium chloride.
4. The method of any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the contacting step is performed in the presence of 0.001 % to 0.4% enzyme, preferably in the presence of 0.05 % to 0.2% enzyme.
5. The method of any one of claims 1 to 4, wherein the contacting step is performed at a pH of from 5 to 8.5; and optionally at a pH of 8.0.
6. The method of any one of claims 1 to 5, wherein the contacting step is performed at a temperature of from about 50 °C to about 70 °C.
7. The method of any one of claims 1 to 6, wherein the enzyme is a protease.

8. The method of any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein the oil-producing microorganisms are selected from the group consisting of algae, fungi, bacteria, and protists, optionally where the fungi is yeast; and optionally wherein the oil-producing microorganisms include Thraustochytrids, optionally wherein the oil-producing microorganisms are selected from the genus Thraustochytrium, Schizochytrium and mixtures thereof.
9. The method of any one of claims 1 to 8, wherein the oil comprises docosahexaenoic acid.
10. The method of any one of claims 1 to 9, wherein the high temperature during the extraction step is from 75°C to 95°C or wherein the high temperature during the extraction step is 85 °C.
11. The method of any one of claims 1 to 10, wherein the concentration step comprises removing a heavy layer from a light layer.
12. The method of any one of claims 1 to 11, wherein 50-95% of the aqueous components are separated from the disrupted microorganisms comprising the oil.
13. The method of any one of claims 1 to 12, wherein 75% to 95% of the oil is recovered; and optionally at least 80% of the oil is recovered or at least 90% of the oil is recovered.

14. The method of any one of claims 1 to 13, wherein the absence of organic solvent means less than about 0.5% solvent based on the weight of the disrupted microorganisms, and optionally wherein the absence of organic solvent means less than 0.4%, 0.3%, 0.2%, 0.1%, 0.05%, 0.01% or 0.005% based on the weight of the disrupted microorganisms or wherein the absence of organic solvent means 0% based on the weight of the disrupted microorganisms.
15. The method of any one of claims 1 to 14, wherein the method is carried out in the absence of surfactants.
